writeup.headline: Akamai rates Hold: steady cash generation and AI cloud wins offset by slow growth, leverage and weak trend.
writeup.thesis: Akamai scores 49, a Hold, sitting just 5 points above the Sell band and 16 points below Buy. Growth is modest, with TTM revenue growth of 5.9% and growth slowed by 0.4 pp from the previous quarter, while quality is middling: an operating margin of 10.5% and FCF margin of 22.1% are offset by stock-based compensation at 11.8% of revenue and diluted share count up 5.8% year on year. In absolute terms valuation is mixed, with P/S of 3.3x and P/FCF of 14.7x looking moderate, EV/EBIT of 40.2x looking high, and FCF yield 1.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield; against its own history it is near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S cheap, P/FCF middle, EV/EBIT expensive). The balance sheet weighs on the score, with net debt at 4.4x FCF and cash covering 0.44 of debt, and the price trend is weak, with the price 39.1% below its 52-week high and 12.8% below its 200-day average. News is mildly positive, helped by over $14B of multiyear cloud contracts and new AI products, though Anthropic dependence is now material.
key_risks: Growing reliance on the Anthropic commitment creates material customer concentration.
Leverage of 4.4x net debt to FCF with cash covering only 0.44 of debt.
Ongoing dilution, with diluted share count up 5.8% year on year and SBC at 11.8% of revenue.
Weak share price trend: 39.1% below its 52-week high and 10.8 pp behind SPY over 126 trading days.
Q3 results and new guidance on Nov 5, 2026 could disappoint after analysts trimmed targets and estimates.
what_would_change: A drop of 5 points in the composite score would move the rating to Sell, for example from a weak Nov 5 report hitting growth or news risk.
Reaching Buy would need 16 more points, likely requiring re-accelerating revenue growth from the TTM 5.9% level alongside a recovering price trend.
Converting the large AI cloud contracts into faster revenue and paying down debt would lift growth and balance sheet scores.
Further share price weakness or rising dilution would pressure trend and quality scores.
